tasks.short: Plan which crew members need which drills, prepare the drill scenario and materials, instruct and drill personnel, and record attendance and results.

steps.what: Fire captain plans drill topics per crew member in a spreadsheet
Fire captain prepares the drill scenario and materials
Fire captain instructs and drills fire department personnel in firefighting, medical care and hazardous materials response
Fire captain records attendance and results on a paper list

tasks.design: The region's training system ({LMS}) holds each firefighter's competence requirements and shows who is due for which drill, so the captain no longer keeps a spreadsheet per crew. Drill scenarios come from the region's shared scenario bank and are adapted to the station's area. Attendance and results are entered on a tablet in the training system during the drill, replacing the paper list typed in later. Instructing and drilling stay with the captain.
tasks.previous_blocker: Due drills were tracked in station spreadsheets and attendance on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Training systems track competence per person and take attendance on tablets.
tasks.human_edge: Pushing a crew harder in a drill so the real incident feels familiar.

evidence.claim: Training systems can track competence requirements per person and register drill attendance on tablets.
Systems that can monitor staff performance need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from competence requirements to the drill record; formal exams are outside.
Input contract: requirements set by the region; scenario bank kept by the training department; fallback is spreadsheets and paper.
Instructing and drilling do not change.
Crew members' time does not change.

incremental.description: Fire captain adds local details to shared scenarios.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small volunteer crew; high: a large station with many crews.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write the vacancy, screen applications, schedule interviews and physical tests, interview candidates, decide on the hire, send offer and rejection letters, and pass the hire to HR.

steps.what: Fire captain writes the vacancy text to recruit firefighting personnel
Fire captain screens applications
Fire captain schedules interviews and physical tests by e-mail
Fire captain interviews candidates
Fire captain decides whom to hire
Fire captain e-mails offer and rejection letters to candidates
Fire captain e-mails the new hire's details to HR for the contract

tasks.design: Vacancies start from HR's template and are published from the applicant tracking system ({ATS}), where applications arrive in one list instead of the captain's inbox. Shortlisted candidates book interview and physical test slots themselves in the system. Screening, interviewing and deciding stay with the captain; no software ranks or rejects candidates. Once the captain has decided, offer and rejection letters go out from templates and the new hire's details pass to HR ({HCM}).
tasks.previous_blocker: Applications came by e-mail, slots were agreed one by one and details retyped for HR.
tasks.enabler_now: Applicant tracking systems handle applications, slot booking and handover to HR.
tasks.still_hard: Few candidates for volunteer and part-time posts.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a candidate will fit a close-knit crew.

evidence.claim: Applicant tracking systems collect applications, let candidates book slots and pass hires to HR.
AI used to screen or rank job applicants is high-risk under Annex III; here no software ranks candidates.

assumptions: Boundary: from the vacancy need to the hire with HR; contracts and onboarding are outside.
Input contract: templates from HR; fallback is e-mail.
Candidates book slots in the system in about the time an e-mail reply took; a little candidate time is priced.
Interviewing and deciding do not change.
research_questions: Does time from vacancy to hire fall?

incremental.description: Fire captain sets up interview slots in the system.
Candidates book their own interview and test slots.

approvals.approved_version: The hire decision taken by the captain in s5.
The hire decision taken by the captain in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one vacancy with few applicants; high: a recruitment round with many candidates.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read building information and water sources on the way, assess the fire, building condition and danger to adjacent buildings on scene, and decide crew and company requirements.

steps.what: Fire captain reads the paper accessibility map and building file in the vehicle
Fire captain assesses nature and extent of fire, condition of building, danger to adjacent buildings and water supply status
Fire captain decides crew or company requirements and requests units by radio

tasks.design: The vehicle's mobile data terminal ({OPS_SYSTEM}) opens the building plan, stored hazardous materials and the nearest hydrants and open water for the incident address, so the captain no longer leafs through the paper map folder on the way. Assessing the scene and deciding on units stay with the captain.
tasks.previous_blocker: Building information sat in paper folders in the vehicle.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile data terminals show building and water information per address.
tasks.still_hard: Building files are often out of date.
tasks.human_edge: Reading smoke colour and movement to judge where the fire is going.

reach.learn: Whether they know the building before arrival.

evidence.claim: Mobile data terminals in fire vehicles can show building plans, hazardous materials and water sources per address.

assumptions: Boundary: from the incident call to units requested; command of the incident is outside.
Input contract: building files and water sources kept by the region's prevention department; fallback is paper folders.
Assessing and deciding do not change.
research_questions: Do captains arrive knowing the nearest water source more often?

incremental.description: Fire captain reports outdated building files after incidents.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly known buildings; high: a large area with many unknown buildings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect invoices and receipts for incident costs, compare spending with the budget, judge whether costs are necessary and reasonable, ask about unclear costs, write the expenditure note, and send it to the station commander.

steps.what: Fire captain collects invoices and receipts for fire suppression costs
Fire captain compares spending with the budget in a spreadsheet
Fire captain monitors whether fire suppression expenditures are necessary and reasonable
Fire captain asks crews and suppliers about unclear costs
Fire captain writes the expenditure note
Fire captain e-mails the note to the station commander

tasks.design: Suppliers' invoices and crew expense claims are booked against the incident number in the finance system ({ERP}), so the captain sees costs per incident instead of collecting documents by e-mail. A budget dashboard ({BI}) shows spending per cost type against the station budget. The expenditure note uses a template with the dashboard figures. Judging whether costs are necessary and asking about unclear ones stay with the captain. Once written, the note goes to the station commander.
tasks.previous_blocker: Invoices and receipts were gathered by e-mail and compared in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Finance systems book costs to incident numbers; budget dashboards are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Large incidents bring costs from many parties weeks later.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing whether a big foam bill was the right call at the time.
tasks.altitude: The captain judges costs instead of collecting them.

reach.learn: Whether incident costs are booked correctly.

evidence.claim: Finance systems can book costs to an incident number and show budgets in dashboards.

assumptions: Boundary: from incident costs to the note sent; budget setting is outside.
Input contract: invoices booked by finance with the incident number; fallback is e-mail and spreadsheets.
Suppliers state the incident number on invoices.
unknowns: Incidents with large costs per year.

incremental.description: Fire captain corrects costs booked to the wrong incident.

approvals.approved_version: The note as written by the captain in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few incidents with costs; high: many incidents with costs from many suppliers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The fire captain keeps drilling crews, interviewing, judging the scene and judging costs; spreadsheets, e-mail rounds and paper folders shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A captain with more time for crews and drills.
